dedupe_keys.name: thermodynamic assessment of a reversible geothermal hthp orc system

description: Tryfonas Roumpedakis and colleagues document a Python model of a geothermal plant operating as a high-temperature heat pump or Organic Rankine Cycle power unit. It combines design-point component sizing with hourly off-design simulation using R1234ze(E). The abstract describes a case with a 105 °C brine inlet, maximum flow of 5.4 kg/s and approximately 800 kW design heat input. It reports heating-led annual performance using a constructed demand profile and real weather data. Zenodo supplies the conference paper freely under CC BY 4.0; this licence applies to the documented publication, while separate code availability and licensing are unknown. Coverage is a described plant case whose location and simulated calendar year are not stated. The related FlexGeo experimental dataset concerns different test equipment. A limitation is that the abstract cannot establish numerical implementation or validation accuracy; no paper body or software was downloaded.
